title: Sandbox microbench & precision pathfinder - Optimize walkthrough
summary: Intro demo of Redwood Optimize sandbox microbench focusing on INT8 vs FP8 precision profiles. Covered baseline metrics, quality delta examples, fallback rules, KV cache effects, and a proposed pilot plan. Customer asked for latency SLO examples, security docs, and a scoped bench to run their clinical prompts.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Ava Martinez: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll give a 45 minute walkthrough but leave time for q's, great to meet NimbusCare team.
[00:00:12] Tom Blake: Hi Ava thanks, excited — we want to see hands on how precision affects our latency and clinical QA thresholds.
[00:00:28] Lucas Chen: awesome, i'm lucas, i'll drive the sandbox microbench demo; quick note: we'll show int8 and fp8 profiles, plus a hybrid fallback.
[00:00:44] Priya Singh: quick qual — our current infra is k8s on GCP, and we mostly call the model in a request/response pattern with 1–2 second tail SLO.
[00:01:03] Ava Martinez: perfect, that helps, and what's your throughput? like p50 vs p95?
[00:01:12] Jordan Reyes: p50 around 180ms for short prompts but p95 spikes to 1.8s during bursts.
[00:01:25] Lucas Chen: okay good, so we'll emphasize tail behavior and stress tests. starting the console — uh screen share — (background noise)
[00:01:42] Speaker 1: (screen) so in the Optimize sandbox, we have a microbench tab. we upload a prompt set, pick models and precision profiles.
[00:02:03] Lucas Chen: here's our baseline run — FP16-ish reference then INT8 profile and FP8 high-fidelity. note the token-per-second throughput and median latency here.
[00:02:25] Lina Gomez: can you point to the metric that captures hallucination rate?
[00:02:33] Rafael Ortiz: yes we show a quality delta using a prompt set, it's a custom eval — fidelity score and a confusion matrix, but it's statistical not perfect.
[00:02:52] Priya Singh: we care about clinical accuracy for a set of 120 prompts, do you support deterministic sampling for comparability?
[00:03:05] Lucas Chen: yep, you can pin seeds or use temperature=0 for deterministic runs; for quality we recommend sampling off to measure diversity then compare factuality metrics.
[00:03:20] [00:03:20] Tom Blake: i see a 12% latency reduction with INT8 but a 3.4% drop in fidelity on the smoking cessation set — is that typical?
[00:03:36] Lucas Chen: somewhere in that neighborhood, yeah — but depends a lot on prompt length, KV cache hit rate, and model architecture. note that FP8 often hits a sweet spot: near-FP16 quality with much of the speedup.
[00:03:52] Ava Martinez: important nuance — we also support a hybrid policy: route 95% of requests to INT8 and 5% to FP8 or FP16 for QA sampling.
[00:04:07] Jordan Reyes: how does KV cache play into that? our conversations with infra teams showed cache misses cause big tails.
[00:04:18] Lucas Chen: good point — prefix/KV cache reduces repeated token generation cost. in the microbench we simulated 30% prefix reuse and saw p95 improvements by about 220ms. sometimes the transcripted logs show "K-V cash" but it's KV cache.
[00:04:38] Priya Singh: any caution on quantization surprises? we saw earlier tests where certain medical terms got munged.
[00:04:48] Rafael Ortiz: yes, that's why qprofiles include per-layer sensitivity sweeps — the sandbox can auto-detect sensitive tokens and create fallback rules for those patterns.
[00:05:06] [00:05:06] Tom Blake: do you have a rollback playbook in case production quality regresses?
[00:05:13] Lucas Chen: absolutely — canary rollout, live A/B, and an automatic failover to a higher-precision variant if fidelity falls below threshold. we log everything to the console traces.
[00:05:28] Priya Singh: what's the integration story with our SSO and KMS? compliance is big for us.
[00:05:36] Ava Martinez: Redwood Private supports your VPC and customer-managed KMS; we have SOC 2 and ISO artifacts — i'll send the package.
[00:05:48] Priya Singh: great.
[00:06:00] [00:06:00] Lucas Chen: hopping back to numbers: here's an INT8 profile with conservative per-layer clamping — we get 1.4x throughput and median latency down from 320ms to 210ms on this sample.
[00:06:20] Lina Gomez: what about outliers? p99?
[00:06:26] Lucas Chen: p99's more sensitive; in our bench p99 sometimes worsens with aggressive batching; that's why we show a heatmap of SLO vs batch size.
[00:06:44] Tom Blake: can we see a live comparison using one of our clinical prompts?
[00:06:51] Ava Martinez: yes — Priya shared a sanitized subset earlier; we'll run that now in the sandbox. starting run...
[00:07:10] [00:07:10] Speaker 2: (typing) okay run complete: FP8 fidelity 0.96 vs INT8 0.92 on the clinical set; latency: FP8 240ms, INT8 170ms median.
[00:07:30] Priya Singh: that 4 point fidelity delta is marginal for some tasks but critical for diagnosis phrasing. can we define threshold-based routing?
[00:07:42] Lucas Chen: yes — route by intent classifier: if prompt classified as "high risk" route to FP8/FP16. we provide SDK hooks for classifier routing.
[00:07:58] Jordan Reyes: curious about cost delta, roughly what unit cost differences do you see?
[00:08:06] Rafael Ortiz: depends on model and infra but INT8 can be 30–45% cheaper per token on GPU pricing compared to FP16; FP8 sits between. sandbox includes cost modeling with your cost assumptions.
[00:08:25] [00:08:25] Tom Blake: any caveats for long context window calls? we do long discharge summaries sometimes.
[00:08:34] Lucas Chen: long sequences amplify quantization error in attention; we recommend targeted per-layer fp override for early layers or using FP8 for long-context endpoints.
[00:08:52] Priya Singh: what's required to run a pilot?
[00:08:58] Ava Martinez: short version: share a sanitized prompt set, we'll provision a sandbox with your model configs, run microbench, and deliver a report with suggested qprofiles and rollout plan.
[00:09:12] Lina Gomez: how long to get sandbox access?
[00:09:16] Maya Patel: usually 2 business days for onboarding, 5–10 days for a full microbench cycle.
[00:09:28] [00:09:28] Tom Blake: okay, timeline sounds workable. can you put the metrics in a format our SREs can ingest?
[00:09:35] Lucas Chen: yes CSV and BigQuery export supported, plus traces in OpenTelemetry.
[00:09:46] Priya Singh: question on fallback complexity: does the runtime do dynamic fallback or is it config based?
[00:09:54] Lucas Chen: both — configs define policies, runtime enforces and can trigger dynamic fallback based on telemetry thresholds.
[00:10:08] [00:10:08] Ava Martinez: quick interjection — competitors asked: Vertex AI has a managed offering, OpenAI for pure-hosted, and some infra shops build custom quant pipelines. our differentiator is integrated profiling + rollout + observability.
[00:10:28] Tom Blake: are there any known failure modes with FP8?
[00:10:33] Rafael Ortiz: FP8 can be unstable in ultra-low-precision kernels for certain heads; we include validation sweeps and conservative fallbacks.
[00:10:47] Priya Singh: would you help tune seeds and sampling for our eval?
[00:10:53] Lucas Chen: yes we'll include a tuning pass and recommendations.
[00:11:04] [00:11:04] Lina Gomez: can the sandbox gem sample traffic from prod for live tests?
[00:11:10] Maya Patel: we support a traffic mirror to the sandbox with consent and safeguards, but typically customers replay sanitized logs.
[00:11:24] Tom Blake: ok let's fast forward to the canary plan example.
[00:11:29] Lucas Chen: slide shows canary: 1% FP8 fallback checks, 5% sample to FP8, rollback threshold at 2 sigma drop in fidelity.
[00:11:46] Priya Singh: and alerting?
[00:11:49] Ava Martinez: we push alerts to PagerDuty and Slack; console has anomaly alerts based on eval metrics.
[00:11:58] [00:11:58] Tom Blake: question — do you retain PII in any logs?
[00:12:04] Ava Martinez: no PII retention by default for hosted — in Private deployments logs can be customer-managed.
[00:12:14] Priya Singh: good.
[00:12:18] [00:12:18] Lucas Chen: demo wrap-up: here's the microbench report — includes fidelity deltas, latency distributions, suggested qprofile JSON and rollout steps.
[00:12:35] Tom Blake: can you share the qprofile JSON so our data science team can review?
[00:12:39] Ava Martinez: yes we'll attach it.
[00:12:45] [00:12:45] Priya Singh: last question on observability — do you expose token-level traces?
[00:12:50] Rafael Ortiz: token-level with sampling, and aggregated token cost breakdown per-call.
[00:13:02] Lina Gomez: nice.
[00:13:07] [00:13:07] Tom Blake: ok next steps?
[00:13:10] Ava Martinez: recap — we'll send: 1) sandbox access & onboarding doc, 2) security package (SOC2/ISO/SAML), 3) sample qprofile and microbench CSV, 4) proposed pilot scope and pricing.
[00:13:30] Jordan Reyes: i'll be the technical point of contact for SRE.
[00:13:35] Priya Singh: i'll be ML contact.
[00:13:40] Ava Martinez: great, we'll follow up with dates; any other questions?
[00:13:45] Tom Blake: none here, thanks.
[00:13:48] [00:13:48] Ava Martinez: thanks everyone — end meeting.

Note: transcription includes minor mis-hearings and abbreviated labels; timestamps approximate. There are intermittent phrases like 'K-V cash' which are transcription artifacts for KV cache.
